current_behavior: CodeMemory already accepts canonical coding events through shared HTTP/CLI paths, extracts candidates, consolidates cards, and verifies Project_J bindings. No cohesive manual agent lifecycle bridge exists yet.
affected_consumers: Existing extraction worker and consolidation service
evidence: README.md lists POST /v1/events, POST /v1/events/batch, cards/search, extraction, consolidation, and verification surfaces.
EventEnvelope already carries producer, project/task/session, seq, context, payload, artifacts, source, and completeness.
CodexHistoryImporter filters host context and hidden reasoning before canonical ingestion.
Phase 4B Project_J baseline and verification service are available for bounded smoke validation.
falsifiers: A bridge bypasses IngestService or writes SQLite directly.
Repeated start/capture/finish requests cannot be replayed idempotently.
The manual capture package cannot produce evidence sufficient for extraction and card query.
A Project_J smoke task cannot complete without a private Codex application API.
recommended_knowledge_routes: Keep the bridge provider-neutral and event-envelope based.
Use three coarse-grained lifecycle operations rather than exposing every internal event as a user action.
Mark summarized/manual evidence as partial or summary instead of claiming full transcript capture.
Leave hook/MCP automation as replaceable transport adapters after the manual path is proven.
unknowns: Which Codex skill/plugin configuration will be available in the target desktop build.
Whether a future agent can emit individual tool events or only a bounded end-of-task package.
How much of the existing large runtime outbox should be drained before a live smoke test.
runtime_or_system_owner: CodeSementicMemory localhost process and Codex project skill; no external agent runtime is mutated.
